goal: Upgrade the web app from Angular 16 to Angular 17. Run the official `ng update` migrations first, then fix what the schematics can't. Adopt the new built-in control-flow syntax (@if/@for/@switch) in straightforward templates, and migrate eligible components to standalone where the official schematic applies. Keep behavior identical and public component APIs unchanged — this is a version upgrade, not a redesign. Do NOT rewrite business logic.
conventions: TypeScript strict mode. Prefer the official Angular migration schematics over hand edits. Behavior-preserving and additive; no public API changes. Match existing ESLint rules and Prettier formatting. Keep the existing module/standalone mix unless a task explicitly migrates a component.

gates.testSetup: Karma/Jasmine via `npm test`. Scope a single spec with `npm test -- --include='**/foo.component.spec.ts' --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`. Requires ChromeHeadless (local Chrome or a CI image). The whole suite must stay green — this upgrade has no intentionally-red phase, so use gate_expectation 'green' for every task.

seed: Run `ng update @angular/core@17 @angular/cli@17`, resolve peer-dep fallout, commit the schematic output. Gate: build + existing tests green.
Apply the official control-flow migration (@if/@for/@switch) to low-risk template groups, one feature area per task.
Migrate eligible components to standalone via the standalone schematic, in dependency order (leaf components first).
Update any deprecated APIs the upgrade surfaced (per build warnings), grouped by subsystem.
